ImageDescription.value:
Wildpark in morning fog, Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The wildlife park was designed in 1864 by English landscape architect Edward Milner as the “Amended Plan of Park Dülmen Westphalia” and laid out in 1868 by Charles Barnard, a gardener who also came from England. It is a classic landscape park with extensive meadows and a system of circular paths, which is also used for forestry. The park features the Herzteich pond with a small island, the moat of the former Schultenhof Hinderkinck farm, and a forester’s lodge near the moat. At the end of the 19th century, among other things, the park was expanded through the acquisition of additional properties. With the construction of the Bundesautobahn 43 in the 1970s, it was reduced in size by approximately 250 hectares.

ImageDescription.value:
Nature reserve “Roruper Holz” (COE-045) in the Hanrorup hamlet near Rorup, Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The Roruper Holz nature reserve is located in the Rorup district of the town of Dülmen in the Münsterland region. It is a near-natural forest area with old trees, wetlands, and structurally rich forest edges.
Typical features include oak and beech trees, as well as small streams and pools that provide habitats for amphibians, insects, and numerous bird species. Deadwood areas promote biodiversity and are particularly valuable from an ecological perspective.

ObjectName.value: Leafs in the winter fog - Flickr - Gael Varoquaux

Categories.value: Fog|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photographs taken on 2020-12-16|Flickr files uploaded by Red panda bot|Photos in Flickr Explore|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation (48° N, 2° E)|Unidentified Fagus|Photographs by Gael Varoquaux

ImageDescription.value:
One foggy morning, in the "bois de Verrière". Seeing that there was thick fog, I went up to take pictures of the woods (fog is great for that).

The elements of the composition are the following: tree trunks form horizontal lines on top of which the branch and leaves contrast by their shape, diagonal direction and non-linearity of the leafs. The colors also contrast, of course, with the red of the leaves contrasting with the blue of the fog. In addition, the light at the center of the picture, with the gap in the trees and the lighter fog, contrasts with the darker, less saturated, and more crowded sides.

The composition ideas to have in mind are that of contrast: the branch is interesting only because it creates a rupture with the monotony of the nearly-vertical trunks; the center appears as light only because the sides are dark.

To create this photo, I found the branch with remaining leafs, of course. But I also choose a spot where there was a gap in the trees (due to a path) and used it to create the less crowded background for the trees.

In terms of post-processing, I used the darktable software to enhace the effects that I was interested in. I made the sides darker and less contrasted. I made the branch more red. I made the fog light in the center. I enhanced the colors, blue and red. My tools where: split-toning for the color, a bit of contrast equalizer (in clarity preset) at the center to add contrast, a few tone curves to set the darkness of trees and background, a bloom filter to create more light, and color correction on the leaves, with a combination of manually-drawn mask and parametric mask (selecting on value) to select the leaves.

Credit.value: Leafs in the winter fog

Artist.value: Gael Varoquaux from Paris, France
